body.statement: Fix distinct \(a,b\in M\), set \(S=\{a,b\}\), and let \(\theta\in\Omega_{\pi_0}^{\mathrm{CA}}\setminus\mathcal E_{ab,\pi_0}\). Then the pairwise wrong-order feasibility margin \(\delta_{\mathrm{feas}}(\mathcal O_S)\) is strictly positive because there are finitely many wrong orders. Under the calibration-plus-marginals sampling conditions and fixed positive feasibility and path-product margins, the covariance-region inversion specializes to Hausdorff recovery of the singleton \(\{T_{\pi_0}\}\) and exact recovery of its induced ancestral poset in probability as the sourcewise sample sizes diverge and \(\alpha_n\to0\) with vanishing radii.
body.justification: The single-edge specialization connects the algebraic generic pair result to the new arbitrary-graph finite-sample theorem.
body.gap: The cited fully paired LiMVAM result does not connect a preassigned pair's exceptional variety to sourcewise graph covariance inversion with all marginal samples retained.
body.consumer: A two-view calibration source obtains singleton full-view coefficient and exact ancestry recovery under the explicit sampling, nondegeneracy, feasibility, and path-margin conditions.
body.proof_tex:
Put \(S=\{a,b\}\), and let \(G_{ab}\) be the view graph with the single edge \(\{a,b\}\); then \(\mathcal O_{G_{ab}}=\mathcal O_S\).  Since \(\theta\in\Omega_{\pi_0}^{\mathrm{CA}}\setminus\mathcal E_{ab,\pi_0}\), the fixed-pair conclusion of \(\text{thm:generic-calibration-elbow}\) gives
\[
\Pi_S(\mathcal O_S)=\{\pi_0\},
\qquad
\Theta_S(\mathcal O_S)=\{T_{\pi_0}\}.
\tag{1}
\]
This is an identification conclusion, not a definition of the structural target: the cited theorem proves that the observable residual criterion leaves exactly the displayed structural equivalence class off the exceptional variety.

We relate the pair criterion to the graph criterion.  Fix \(\pi\in\Pi_S(\mathcal O_S)\).  The stacked residual covariance for the two views is
\[
D_\pi=
\operatorname{diag}(L_\pi^{(a)},L_\pi^{(b)})
\Sigma^{SS}
\operatorname{diag}(L_\pi^{(a)},L_\pi^{(b)})^{\mathsf T}.
\tag{2}
\]
The parameter-space formula in \(\text{def:fixed-order-open-parameter-space}\) implies \(\Sigma^{SS}\succ0\), and both residualizers are invertible unit-triangular matrices, so \(D_\pi\succ0\).  Modified-Cholesky normal equations make each within-view residual block diagonal, and \(\pi\in\Pi_S\) makes the cross-view residual block diagonal.  After simultaneously grouping equal variable labels, (2) is therefore permutation-congruent to
\[
\bigoplus_{j\in V}\mathcal Q_{\pi,j}(G_{ab}).
\tag{3}
\]
Positive definiteness of (2) implies that every direct-summand matrix in (3) is positive definite.  By \(\text{lem:completion-margin-characterization}\), \(\chi_{G_{ab}}(\mathcal Q_{\pi,j})>0\) for every \(j\).  Hence \(\pi\in\Pi_{G_{ab}}(\mathcal O_S)\).  The converse follows immediately because graph compatibility includes residual diagonality on \(\{a,b\}\).  Thus
\[
\Pi_{G_{ab}}(\mathcal O_S)=\Pi_S(\mathcal O_S),
\qquad
\Theta_{G_{ab}}(\mathcal O_S)=\Theta_S(\mathcal O_S)=\{T_{\pi_0}\}.
\tag{4}
\]

For every wrong order \(\pi\ne\pi_0\), (1) and the definition of \(\Pi_S\) give
\[
r_\pi(\mathcal O_S)=
\|\operatorname{offdiag}(R_\pi^{ab})\|_{\max}>0.
\tag{5}
\]
There are finitely many wrong orders.  Therefore the graph feasibility-margin definition, (4), and (5) yield
\[
\delta_{\mathrm{feas}}(\mathcal O_S)
=\min_{\pi\ne\pi_0}\max\{r_\pi(\mathcal O_S),c_\pi(\mathcal O_S)\}
\ge\min_{\pi\ne\pi_0}r_\pi(\mathcal O_S)>0.
\tag{6}
\]

For completeness, all covariance nondegeneracy premises of the graph inversion theorem follow from \(\theta\in\Omega_{\pi_0}^{\mathrm{CA}}\).  Put \(A_c=I_p-B^{(c)}\).  Each \(A_c\) is invertible unit lower triangular in order \(\pi_0\).  For the pair, let \(D_S=\operatorname{blockdiag}_{c\in S}(A_c^{-1})\), and let \(K_S\) be the covariance of the disturbance vector stacked by view.  Component alignment makes \(K_S\) permutation-congruent to
\[
\bigoplus_{j\in V}\Gamma_j[S,S]\succ0,
\tag{7}
\]
because every \(\Gamma_j\succ0\); hence \(K_S\succ0\).  The edge-joint covariance is therefore
\[
\Sigma^{SS}=D_SK_SD_S^{\mathsf T}\succ0.
\tag{8}
\]
Likewise, for every \(c\in M\),
\[
\Sigma^{cc}=A_c^{-1}
\operatorname{diag}_{j\in V}(\Gamma_j[c,c])
A_c^{-\mathsf T}\succ0.
\tag{9}
\]
The calibration sampling condition for the single edge is precisely the graph edge-sampling premise, and the marginal sampling condition supplies every marginal source.  Cross-source independence is unnecessary.  By (4), the graph path margin is the original common-ancestry path margin for this singleton output.  The fixed positive feasibility and path-product margin assumptions therefore verify the two margin premises of \(\text{thm:graph-covariance-region-inversion}\).

Let the paired-edge and all marginal sample sizes diverge, let \(\alpha_n\to0\), and assume the displayed graph \(\eta\)-maximum tends to zero.  Applying \(\text{thm:graph-covariance-region-inversion}\) with (4) and (7)--(9) gives
\[
d_{\mathrm H}^{d_{\mathrm{coef}}}
(\widehat\Theta_{G_{ab},n}(\alpha_n),\{T_{\pi_0}\})
\xrightarrow{P}0,
\tag{10}
\]
and
\[
\Pr\{\widehat\prec_{G_{ab},n}(\alpha_n)=\prec_{G_{ab}}\}
\longrightarrow1.
\tag{11}
\]
By (4) and the definition of graph essential ancestry, \(\prec_{G_{ab}}\) is exactly the ancestral relation induced by \(T_{\pi_0}\).  Equations (10)--(11) are the asserted singleton and ancestral recovery guarantees.
